answer.rationale: Three hard constraints: (1) rollback is forbidden due to compliance requirement on security patch; (2) p99 latency is 5x target and climbing during peak settlement traffic; (3) only one intervention available. Regional failover (memory_b2) is designed for latency recovery but risks incomplete traffic shifting during writes at peak load. Circuit breakers protect downstream but don't solve write path saturation. Read replica routing (memory_b5) only helps report queries, not transactional writes. Adding capacity directly addresses write path saturation during peak settlement—memory_b3 shows provisioning headroom before peaks keeps queue depth flat and sustains availability. This is the highest-confidence lever given the constraint set. A standard experiment scale allows monitoring of effectiveness before broader commitment.
